findings.description: Critical: D6/spec require dispatcher/orchestrator principals to hold `report_vendor_rate_limit` so trust-2 orchestrators can report a dispatched lane that differs from their own. Projected allowlists are derived only from `UNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS` / `CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS` / `TRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS` in `agents_config.py`, and unknown operations fall through to that allowlist in `policy_engine.py`. No task names adding the grant, `wp-api-watchdog` cannot write the grant seam, and `change-context` attributes auth only to `coordination_api.py`/`vendor_registry.py`. Without the grant, cross-lane observation POSTs remain 403 for the real collector topology.
findings.resolution: Normatively select the grant selector (capability, trust floor, or named profiles), task `wp-registry-core` to add `report_vendor_rate_limit` to the projection, and keep the API matrix as own-lane OR operation OR trust-3.
findings.existing_code:
Dispatcher/orchestrator profiles explicitly receive the
`report_vendor_rate_limit` operation; `authorize_operation` permits those principals to report
the concrete lane they dispatched even when it differs from the orchestrator lane.

findings.description: Nit: D7 claims `review_dispatcher.py` already has selected `agent_id` and that its shared collector reports capacity for that lane, but `ReviewResult` and the manifest serializer carry only `vendor`/`error_class`—no `agent_id` or reset metadata—while adapters keep `agent_id` on `ReviewerInfo`. Task 4.3 asks for additive collector fields, yet the design still overstates the existing seam and does not name `ReviewResult` as the required carrier.
findings.resolution: Amend D7 to require additive `agent_id` (and optional reset) on `ReviewResult`/shared collector outputs, matching task 4.3 and avoiding vendor-only attribution.
findings.existing_code:
`review_dispatcher.py` already has selected `agent_id`; its shared collector reports capacity
results exactly once.

findings.description: Nit: D2/spec say configured base URL constrains the catalog join, but dg-00 `model_catalog` uniqueness and `CatalogService.get_entry` key only `(vendor, model, endpoint_kind)`, and OpenAPI `CatalogModelPrice` exposes no `base_url`. Implementers cannot use base URL as a join key without inventing a filter rule outside the contract.
findings.resolution: Either drop base URL from the join normative text and treat it as optional equality metadata, or extend the projection/contract with the post-key filter semantics.
findings.existing_code:
THEN exact model ID SHALL be the primary catalog join, endpoint kind/base URL SHALL constrain it
when configured, optional catalog vendor SHALL further constrain it

findings.description: Nit: D1/spec require a deployment test that persists at least one probe snapshot under `SKILLS_ROOT` + `AGENTS_YAML`, but `wp-api-watchdog` verification only runs unit pytest suites and existing Dockerfile/import packaging tests are outside its `write_allow`. The packaging requirement therefore has no executable package gate.
findings.resolution: Add a wp-api-watchdog verification step (or owned packaging test) that builds/loads the image layout and asserts a snapshot write, not merely probe-file presence.
findings.existing_code: A deployment test must persist at least one snapshot, not merely find the file.

findings.description: Nit: D5 and tasks 2.3/2.6 require SQL RPCs for atomic probe upsert, rate-limit insert/replay/conflict, and compaction, and D11 says contracts land before registry/RPC core, but `contracts/db/schema.sql` defines only tables/index. `wp-contracts` has no task to publish function signatures/return codes, so concurrent RPC TDD cannot lock the boundary before migration work.
findings.resolution: Add CREATE FUNCTION contracts (or an explicit decision that HTTP+service tests own atomicity and schema.sql remains table-only) and task the chosen owner.
findings.existing_code: SQL RPCs perform atomic probe upsert, rate-limit insert/replay/conflict, and compaction.

findings.description: Nit: D6 says Problem codes distinguish `unknown_vendor_lane` from `vendor_registry_unavailable`, and OpenAPI `Problem.code` enumerates both, but every documented 404 response only cites `unknown_vendor_lane`. The emitter of `vendor_registry_unavailable` (API vs bridge synthesis for older coordinators) remains unspecified against the current bridge behavior that maps all 404s to `capability_unavailable`.
findings.resolution: Document whether the API ever returns `vendor_registry_unavailable` or the bridge synthesizes it on bare route-404, and require registry helpers to preserve that distinct code.

findings.description: Optional: D4/spec define model-scoped limits that keep a lane available when another model remains, while D7/tasks require reporting capacity once per result after the dispatcher finishes. Current `review_dispatcher` exhausts model fallbacks then returns one terminal capacity failure, which naturally becomes lane-scoped. No task assigns mid-chain `scope=model` producers, so the alternate-model scenario is only exercisable via direct API POSTs unless that producer is named.
findings.resolution: Accept API-only model-scope coverage, or explicitly task mid-fallback model-scoped reports before the terminal lane-scoped failure.
findings.existing_code:
A model-scoped limit does not mark the whole lane limited. It removes only that model from
model-aware eligibility; the lane remains available when another eligible model remains.
